metaDesc: A one-day Ang Thong trip from Bangkok, Thailand: the country's tallest Big Buddha at Wat Muang, the 50m reclining Buddha at Wat Khun Inthapramun, plus famous boat-noodle stops, with opening hours and an easy driving loop.

h1:
Ang Thong in One Day
Big Buddha, Reclining Buddha & Food Along the Way
intro: Ang Thong is a low-key province less than two hours' drive from Bangkok, perfect for a single-day temple run there and back. The headliners are the tallest Buddha image in Thailand at Wat Muang and the 50-metre open-air reclining Buddha at Wat Khun Inthapramun, with a stop for famous boat noodles slotted in between. We've ordered everything so the drive flows in one smooth loop, with no doubling back.

blocks.html: Ang Thong sits about 100 kilometres from Bangkok. Take the Asia Highway (Route 32) and you'll be there in roughly an hour and a half. Leave home around 7am and you'll reach the first temple just as it opens, before the sun gets harsh, which makes for great Big Buddha photos. This plan assumes you're driving yourself, since the sights are spread across different districts and connecting by public transport is a hassle.

items: Total distance — Bangkok–Ang Thong round trip is about 220 km, plus another 40 km or so looping around the province.
Time needed — Leave in the morning, head home in the evening, and you'll hit every stop without rushing.
Budget per person — Fuel + food + temple donations, around 400–700 THB (most temples don't charge admission).
What to wear — This is a temple trip, so wear sleeves and trousers or a skirt that covers the knees.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Wat Muang is open 06:00–18:00. Wat Khun Inthapramun opens around 08:00–17:00, so put it in the late-morning-to-afternoon slot to match its hours rather than arriving too early before it's ready for visitors.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Big Buddha, Reclining Buddha, and food along the way

items.activity: Leave Bangkok and get on the Asia Highway (Route 32)
items.note: Stop for a restroom break or coffee at a petrol station on the way. Traffic is still light at this hour.

items.activity: Arrive at Wat Muang in Wiset Chai Chan district to pay respects to Luang Pho Yai, the largest Buddha image in Thailand
items.note: The lap is 62m wide and the image stands about 93m tall, with stairs up for a closer view. Open 06:00–18:00, no admission fee.

items.activity: Walk the grounds of Wat Muang — the model heaven-and-hell garden, the lotus-petal glass wall, and photo angles of the Big Buddha
items.note: The morning sun is still soft, so the white image stands out nicely against the sky.

items.activity: Drive into Ang Thong town for a late-morning bowl of boat noodles
items.note: The town has several well-known boat-noodle shops. Small bowls start around 20 THB, so ordering several is no problem.

items.activity: Head to Pho Thong district to pay respects to the reclining Buddha at Wat Khun Inthapramun
items.note: This open-air reclining Buddha is 50m long and dates back to the Sukhothai era. Open around 08:00–17:00.

items.activity: Stop for lunch around Pho Thong or Pa Mok, then visit Wat Pa Mok Worawihan
items.note: Wat Pa Mok has an Ayutthaya-era reclining Buddha about 24m long beside the Chao Phraya River, conveniently on the way back to Bangkok.

items.activity: Stop at Ban Bang Sadet to see the court-style dolls and handmade souvenirs
items.note: A riverside handicraft village on the Chao Phraya, where you can pick up terracotta dolls and keepsakes to take home.

items.activity: Start the drive back to Bangkok
items.note: You'll be home around 17:00–17:30, ahead of the evening traffic.

blocks.text: Boat Noodles & Food Along the Way

blocks.html: The food people associate with Ang Thong is boat noodles — rich broth in small, wallet-friendly bowls that you order several of at once, which is completely normal here. These are the shops that locals and visitors mention most often, picked from real reviews.

items.name: Ruea Thong Boat Noodles (near the monument)
items.blurb: A big place with plenty of seating and a constant stream of customers, serving both tom yum and clear-broth boat noodles. The broth is well-balanced and small bowls are cheap, making it a great late-morning stop along the way.
items.meta: Boat noodles · small bowls from about ฿20

items.name: Tiao Ruea Yutya (in front of Ang Thong Hospital)
items.blurb: A favourite of Ang Thong locals, with a bold broth you won't need to season. There's nam tok, tom yum, and clear broth, plus a standout side of braised pork rice stir-fried with kaffir lime leaves. Open around 08:30–17:00.
items.meta: Boat noodles · Pho Sa subdistrict, Mueang district

items.name: Sane Ang Thong Boat Noodles
items.blurb: A local boat-noodle shop with tom yum, clear broth, and pad thai at reasonable prices. Good for a quick bite before heading to the next temple.
items.meta: Boat noodles & pad thai · in town

items.name: Po Prateep Boat Noodles
items.blurb: On the Ang Thong–Pa Mok road in Sala Daeng subdistrict, right on the route to and from Pa Mok, so it's an easy stop on the way back.
items.meta: Boat noodles · Ang Thong–Pa Mok road

items.name: Tom Yum Noodles at the Pa Mok Bend
items.blurb: A homely shop right on the bend heading to Pa Mok, known for its tom yum noodles with minced pork, offal, soft-boiled egg, and crispy wontons. Easy on the budget.
items.meta: Tom yum noodles · on the way to Pa Mok

blocks.title: Tips for eating
blocks.html: Small boat-noodle bowls go down well 3–4 at a time, so save some room to try the duck rice or steamed coconut custard many shops also serve. Most shops in town close in the late afternoon, so check the hours first if you're planning to eat there for dinner.

blocks.text: Extra Stops If You Have Time

items.name: Wat Ton Son
items.blurb: In Ang Thong town, home to Somdet Phra Si Mueang Thong, a large gilded and lacquered cast-metal Buddha image. An easy stop to pay respects along the way.

items.name: Ban Bang Sadet Court Doll Museum
items.blurb: A Thai-style building beside the Chao Phraya where you can watch court dolls being made and buy local handicraft souvenirs.

items.name: Wat Pa Mok Worawihan
items.blurb: An Ayutthaya-era reclining Buddha about 24m long beside the Chao Phraya River, on the way back to Bangkok — a good stop to close out the trip.

items: Self-drive — The easiest option. Take Route 32 (the Asia Highway), then turn off into the province. The main temples have large car parks.
Van / coach — There are services from Mo Chit to Ang Thong town, but getting around the province means catching songthaews or hiring a vehicle, which isn't ideal for a single day.
Pair it with Ayutthaya — Ang Thong borders Ayutthaya, so if you have two days you can combine both provinces into one trip.
Avoid long holidays — Wat Muang gets very crowded during festivals. If you want relaxed photos, go on a weekday instead.

faq.q: Is one day enough for Ang Thong?
faq.a: Easily. Ang Thong is a small province, and the main sights like Wat Muang and Wat Khun Inthapramun aren't far apart by car. Leave Bangkok in the morning and head back in the evening, and you'll cover the Big Buddha, the reclining Buddha, and a boat-noodle stop along the way.

faq.q: What are Wat Muang's opening hours, and is there an admission fee?
faq.a: Wat Muang is open daily, roughly 06:00–18:00, with no admission fee — donations are up to you. Going in the morning, before the sun gets harsh, means better Big Buddha photos and fewer crowds.

faq.q: Are Wat Muang and Wat Khun Inthapramun far apart?
faq.a: Wat Muang is in Wiset Chai Chan district and Wat Khun Inthapramun is in Pho Thong district, about 30–40 minutes' drive apart through the town centre. A boat-noodle stop in town fits perfectly in between.

faq.q: How long is the drive to Ang Thong from Bangkok?
faq.a: About an hour and a half if traffic is light, via Route 32 (the Asia Highway), a distance of roughly 100 kilometres. It's a close, convenient temple trip you can do there and back in a single day.

faq.q: What food should you try in Ang Thong?
faq.a: Boat noodles are the local specialty — rich broth in small bowls starting around 20 THB, so you can order several. There are well-known shops near the monument, in front of the hospital, and on the road to Pa Mok.
